subject: Pod #010 — The line they would not cross
previewText: LD-12 has detected two weapons, one illegal refusal, and a fist bump with catastrophic long-term consequences.
heading: The Line They Would Not Cross
deck: Seven cards. Two impossible weapons. One order refused. The partnership becomes family.

hero.alt: Moon Gun Sam release-week poster showing Sam, Kelli, their family, Kuranis, and hooded enemies

opening.title: Hey Pod. The books are loose.
copy: The Dolphin — Vow and The Dolphin — Ember arrived three days ago. So this is not a normal transmission. This is the release-week armory dump: seven cards, two weapons, one terrible command, and the moment Sam and Alex decide what kind of Moon Guns they are willing to become.

Training gives them the VXG-76 and Psalm—enough power to breach walls, tear armor, and end a fight in several deeply discouraging colors. What matters is what happens when Fenyang orders Alex to use that power on a defeated opponent.
She refuses. Sam stands beside her. Everything after that grows from the line they draw together.

cards.title: The Moon Gun VXG-76
cards.alt: Trading card showing the VXG-76 Moon Gun weapon
copy: The VXG-76 is massive, brutal, and inconveniently versatile. Breach tears through walls and can throw its operator clear. Bolt drives focused shots through hard targets. Shear turns the weapon into something resembling a very bad argument with a shotgun.

Multi tracks several targets at once. Grapple restrains, climbs, or drags a problem closer. Plasma can jump between harmonic weapons, although sensible operators avoid discovering why that mode is rarely used. This is the machine Sam and Alex are expected to master without letting it master them.

cards.title: The Tonfa Machette — Psalm
cards.alt: Trading card showing Psalm, the harmonic tonfa machette
copy: Before recruits earn a Moon Gun, they train with Psalm: a harmonic tonfa machette whose edge does not run out of ammunition and whose colors are less decorative than they appear.

Red tears. Black leaves rot behind. Green poisons. Blue freezes. White burns and seals. Every mode can chew through tissue, armor, or bone; every counter can wreck the attacker's balance before the blade ever lands. Psalm teaches the lesson the VXG will later enforce: power is never only what you can do. It is what you decide not to do.

cards.title: Klein vs. Jamestown
cards.alt: Trading card showing Alex Klein fighting the much larger Jamestown
copy: Alex is matched against Jamestown, a recruit built like a structural concern. She cannot overpower him, so she dismantles the problem with speed, timing, and spite. She gets him down. She wins.
Then Jamestown lashes out from the ground and tears open her leg. Alex answers with one final strike that leaves him unconscious. The fight is over. The question is whether she knows when to stop.

cards.title: Disobedience
cards.alt: Trading card showing Alex refusing Fenyang's order while Sam stands beside her
copy: Fenyang orders Alex to kill the defeated Jamestown. Alex throws down Psalm and refuses. Sam steps forward before caution can catch him, furious on behalf of the partner who has already proved everything that needed proving.

Kuranis allows the outburst, then sends them to the medic. The command structure records disobedience. Sam and Alex record something else: there are orders they will not obey, and neither of them will have to refuse alone.

cards.title: Cool Down
cards.alt: Trading card showing Sam keeping Alex company while her leg is treated
copy: Medic Proctor seals the wound in Alex's leg while Sam stays close enough to be irritating. He is openly impressed that she brought down Jamestown. Alex jokes through the pain because sincerity is more dangerous than the blade was.
The adrenaline drains away. The refusal remains. So does Sam.

cards.title: Fist Bump
cards.alt: Trading card showing Sam and Alex sealing their pact with a fist bump
copy: They make the rules the MGU forgot to give them. They will not kill because someone with rank finds it convenient. They will decide where the line is, and when the line costs them, they will pay together.
The agreement is sealed with a fist bump—an alarmingly small gesture for a pact that will eventually inconvenience governments, armies, gods, and at least one administrative intelligence.

cards.title: Sam and Alex — Training Days
cards.alt: Trading card showing Sam and Alex smiling together during their training days
copy: Somewhere between punishments, bruises, and shared acts of insubordination, Sam and Alex stop being two recruits assigned to the same unit. They become a single fighting system. Then something stronger than that: family.

They do not know yet how far their bond will reach. They only know the person beside them will stay when staying becomes expensive. Two hearts, one line, and a future large enough to change the universe.

weaponPlatform.title: The Moon Gun VXG-76
copy: In the field, officers usually call it the VXG or the 76—partly for speed, partly because shouting ‘Moon Gun’ in a squad of Moon Gun Officers creates avoidable administrative comedy. It is not a firearm. It is a modular harmonic platform that channels the same physics as Psalms and the Pools through pulse-capacitor bolts.

The weapon is massive, dark, heavy, and intimidating on purpose. A reinforced back-harness supports its weight, feeds ammunition, stabilizes kick, and compensates for recoil. Microthrusters lighten the system in the air; on the ground, some modes still require the officer to plant their stance and negotiate directly with momentum.
weaponPlatform.harness: 1,000 compressed pulse-capacitor bolts in the reinforced back reservoir.
weaponPlatform.chamber: 100 bolts staged and ready to fire.
weaponPlatform.control: Side-mounted mode selector with HUD cooldowns, target locks, and resonance warnings.

modes.name: BREACH
modes.copy: Sonic-magnetic demolition and displacement. Tears steel, crushes barricades, and launches the officer when fired downward. Thirty-second cooldown; brace on the ground.

modes.name: GRAPPLE
modes.copy: Fifty-meter magnetic tow-line. Climbs, rescues, detains, or pulls targets toward the weapon. Physics determines whether the result remains nonlethal.

modes.name: BOLT
modes.copy: Single explosive pulse-capacitor, detonated on the second trigger pull. Accepts any primary Psalm color or fires as a heavy conventional explosive.

modes.name: MULTI
modes.copy: Locks up to ten targets and fires sequential bolts. Each target receives the selected Psalm effect, assuming the operator considers that helpful.

modes.name: BOLT SHEAR
modes.copy: Splits one bolt into roughly fifty resonant micro-shards for rapid suppression. Loud, messy, and doctrinally associated with officers having a difficult afternoon.

modes.name: PLASMA
modes.copy: Surgical heat beam for precision cuts and anti-armor work. Arcs near active Psalms or other VXGs, creating electrocution and secondary discharge hazards.

weaponPlatform.psalmBolts: Red bleeds, Black blooms into rot, Green poisons, Blue freezes tissue and bone, and White cauterizes and burns. Combo colors cannot survive the casing. Operators prefer Red and White; wider-area colors require sealed armor and better judgment.
weaponPlatform.safety: A Breach shot can collapse a small house. Grapple can convert rescue equipment into immediate anatomy problems. Plasma seeks nearby harmonic weapons. Improper use may cause death, dismemberment, or worse; LD-12 is awaiting clarification on ‘worse.’

armory.title: The Wheel of Psalms
copy: Psalm is not a laser sword. It is a paired T-MACH unit—a tonfa-machette built around pulse-alloy blades and coded harmonic frequencies. Either hilt can select a mode where the fingers settle: index for Red, middle for Black, ring for Green, little finger for Blue, or all four for White.

Every color has two jobs. Its offensive frequency causes a specific injury; its defensive counter stops another frequency in the Wheel. A trained operator changes colors before impact. The built-in double-squeeze shortcut can find the counter automatically, but it is slower—and slow is a poor quality in a weapon that can give tissue opinions.
The thumb control rotates the tonfa grip through four fighting positions for advanced spin-blade techniques. This is not recommended for anyone who enjoys remaining upright, symmetrical, or employed.
armory.sequence: Red → Black → Green → Blue → White → Red. Color is consequence. Remember which sin eats which.
armory.advanced: Elite practitioners can combine modes: Yellow acid spray, Navy devour, Gray breach, Purple electrocution, and Orange flame funnel. A combo can only be stopped by its opposite—or by the same combination performed with cleaner rhythm.
armory.safety: Incorrect rhythm may cause harmonic ricochet, tissue blowback, bone whip, or electrostatic pulse. The phrase ‘advanced spin-blade technique’ is not recognized as a workers’ compensation category.

readerQuestion: Which changes everything: the weapon, the refusal, the staying, or the fist bump?

interview.title: Management interview interrupted by a ten-year-old
interview.alt: LD-12 interviewing Tony during a family card game at Randolph House

lines.speaker: LD-12
lines.text: Management, this interview concerns your irresponsible decision to distribute detailed weapons specifications to civilians.

lines.speaker: TONY
lines.text: They're readers.

lines.speaker: LILA
lines.text: He means nerds.

lines.speaker: ALEX
lines.text: She's right. Also, your turn, toaster.

lines.speaker: LD-12
lines.text: I am conducting an interrogation. I cannot simultaneously participate in recreational deception.

lines.speaker: LILA
lines.text: Then fold.

lines.speaker: LD-12
lines.text: I possess three queens. Folding would be mathematically irrational.

lines.speaker: ALEX
lines.text: No, you don't.

lines.speaker: LD-12
lines.text: You cannot know that.

lines.speaker: ALEX
lines.text: Your left antenna twitches when you bluff.

lines.speaker: LILA
lines.text: It really does. Raise.

lines.speaker: SAM
lines.text: Maybe we should let LD-12 finish the interview.

lines.speaker: KELLI
lines.text: Or you could take me upstairs and explain the VXG recoil harness very slowly.

lines.speaker: SAM
lines.text: We have a ten-year-old at the table.

lines.speaker: LILA
lines.text: I'm ten, not deaf. Also, raise again.

lines.speaker: TONY
lines.text: For the record, Sam was trying to remove Kelli from the interview.

lines.speaker: KELLI
lines.text: No, he wasn't.

lines.speaker: SAM
lines.text: No, I wasn't.

lines.speaker: LD-12
lines.text: Management's account has been contradicted by two primary sources. This is precisely why I conduct interviews.

lines.speaker: ALEX
lines.text: Lila, you're dealing from the bottom.

lines.speaker: LILA
lines.text: I don't cheat.

lines.speaker: ALEX
lines.text: Yeah, you are. I taught you that trick.

lines.speaker: LILA
lines.text: Oh. Yeah. Ha ha ha.

lines.speaker: LD-12
lines.text: CHEATING INVALIDATES THE ENTIRE DATA SET.

lines.speaker: LILA
lines.text: No, it means I win.

lines.speaker: LD-12
lines.text: I demand an immediate rematch under laboratory conditions.

lines.speaker: ALEX
lines.text: Double or nothing, toaster.

lines.speaker: LD-12
lines.text: Accepted. Management, remain seated. Your interview will resume after I restore statistical justice.

fieldReport.title: Operation: Garment Bag Burial
fieldReport.alt: Kelli, Susan, Alex, and Sam laughing together in a wedding boutique
copy: The attached surveillance depicts Kelli Day selecting veil, lace, lilies, and related ceremonial equipment for her forthcoming marriage to Sergeant Sam Randolph. The primary wedding dress is not present. Day intends to wear her mother's dress, converting this mission from garment acquisition to historical-dress augmentation. LD-12 recognizes the sentimental value but requests proof that inherited clothing has passed structural inspection.

Sergeant Randolph has been buried to the chin in garment bags and converted into a mobile supply rack. He describes the boutique as enemy territory, maintains a disciplined expression while Day models lace, and responds to Alexis Klein's commentary with language unsuitable for a bridal establishment. Klein subsequently threatens to wash his mouth out with a Psalm on Red. This is not an approved cleaning application.

Susan Adams is transporting a tower of veils while operating under the influence of three glasses of shop bubbly. She collides with a clothing rack, misplaces personal effects often enough that staff issue a badge-removal warning, and claims Irish resilience as a mitigating factor. It is not.

A later recording contains an additional disclosure: Klein attempted to hire this unit for a bachelorette-party entertainment package. The engagement was declined due to a scheduling conflict at the mechanic shop, an active private investigation, two coffee-shop shifts, and preparations to exercise this unit's authority as an ordained minister. The exact nature of the entertainment package has been classified for the protection of the Pod. Recommendation: approve the wedding, reinforce Randolph's load-bearing capacity, confiscate Susan's fourth drink, and remind Klein that premium bookings require a deposit.

authorNote.title: Well, the books are finally available!
copy: This is a big celebratory newsletter with a lot of lore. You'll find details about the weapons systems here because the books only go into as much detail as the story needs. If you enjoy those kinds of world-building items, dig in. If you're here for the romance and family love, you may glaze over them with my full permission.

This issue finds Sam and Alex in Moon Gun basic training. There is a little of that in Vow because the Moon Guns are the military and police of Luna. The story has those elements, but it isn't really a military science-fiction novel.

This is still an emotional journey, so don't worry. I love the science fantasy and the speculative slant. I enjoy the realism of these first three books. After that, it gets big—full-on space opera—but I promise not to lose the heart of the thing. My main objective is to create characters you love and want to hang out with.
So fall in love. Begin the adventure. Then leave me an honest review on Amazon or Goodreads—or both!
Book Three will be available for preorder soon. Book Four will be announced then as well.
Thank you to everyone in the Pod. It's going to be a fun year!

launchCopy: The Dolphin — Vow and The Dolphin — Ember are out now. Two volumes, one enormous opening movement, and the family whose first rules were written in a training room when an order crossed the line.
If you have followed these cards from the orphanage to Shackleton, this is where the doors finally open. Thank you for walking all the way here with me.
